problem: The projection of the intersection between the elliptic cylinder $9{x}^{2}+2(y-1)^{2}=18$ and the plane $z=1$ onto the $xy$-plane is an ellipse. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the ellipse?

feedback.problem: The projection of the intersection between the hyperbolic cylinder $2(x+6)^{2}-5{y}^{2}=10$ and the plane $z=5$ onto the $xy$-plane is a hyperbola. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the hyperbola?
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the cylinder and the plane $z=5,$ we substitute $z=5$ into the equation of the cylinder. However, since the equation has no (explicit) $z$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+6)^{2}-5{y}^{2} & =10 \\ \frac{(x+6)^{2}}{5}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+6)^{2}}{(\sqrt{5})^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of a hyperbola with semi-axes of lengths $\sqrt{5}$ and $\sqrt{2}.$
